about: The Story Library's Classics shelf (docs/decisions.md "Story Library: a Classics shelf"; docs/story-library-classics.md, written by scripts/import-classics.js). Public-domain illustrated editions, read in full by a person for ages 4 to 10 with the library's content rules. Each source records the edition, its first publication year and every maker's death year (the public-domain rule: published before 1931 and every maker dead before 1956). Questions point at a phrase on the page that answers them (the importer works out the page). Fixes correct clear typos only, each found exactly once.

skipped.14848:The Story of Miss Moppet: Its first sentence calls the kitten "a Pussy" (the old word for a cat); today the word reads as rude to many parents and the site's word filter flags it, and the author's words are not ours to change.
skipped.15137:The Tale of Mrs. Tiggy-Winkle: Several old names and words read as rude today and the site's word filter flags them ("Cock Robin" twice, "little dicky shirt-fronts", "Tom Titmouse"), and the author's words are not ours to change; the copy that was transcribed is also a 1986 printing.
skipped.32488:How the Rhinoceros Got His Skin: Calls the Parsee man's hat "more-than-oriental splendour" three times (exotic labels on a real people), and the Rhinoceros's greeting "How!" reads as a mock Native American word.
skipped.32488:How the Leopard Got His Spots: Uses a racial slur and describes a man by his skin color.
skipped.32488:The Elephant's Child: The child is spanked by every relative all through the story, and spanks them back at the end: hitting children as a running joke.
skipped.32488:How the First Letter Was Written: Taffy's name means "ought to be spanked" and "she was not spanked half as much as was good for her"; the tribe attacks a stranger.
skipped.32488:How the Alphabet Was Made: Follows on from the First Letter story (left out) and depends on about 20 small drawings set inside its sentences, which a page with one picture cannot show.
skipped.32488:The Crab That Played with the Sea: "They shall be called the Malazy, the lazy people": a slur on Malay people.
skipped.32488:The Cat That Walked by Himself: Ends by saying proper men "will always throw things at a Cat" and dogs chase him up a tree: cruelty to animals shown as right.
skipped.32488:The Butterfly That Stamped: A king with 999 quarrelsome wives: plural marriage and wives mocked as a group.
skipped.32488:The poems between the stories: Not part of the stories; left out (some mention ship lines and places only a grown-up would know).
skipped.14407:The Tale of Benjamin Bunny: Old Mr. Bunny whips his son with a switch and smokes a pipe; he kicks the cat.
skipped.14837:The Tale of Tom Kitten: The mother smacks the kittens and tells her friends a lie.
skipped.14872:The Tale of Squirrel Nutkin: The owl holds Nutkin "intending to skin him" and his tail breaks off; dead mice and a mole are brought as presents.
skipped.14814:The Tale of Jemima Puddle-Duck: A fight offstage ends the fox ("nothing more was ever seen"), the dogs are hurt and the puppies eat the eggs.
skipped.15284:The Tale of Johnny Town-Mouse: "The cat had killed the canary", and the cook calls for a poker to kill the mouse.
skipped.15234:The Tale of the Pie and the Patty-: Built around a pie made of mice, and a cat who "died of a thimble".
skipped.14220:The Tale of the Flopsy Bunnies: "I shall skin them and cut off their heads"; a bunny is hit by a thrown marrow.
skipped.14868:The Tailor of Gloucester: The cat traps mice under teacups to eat them; a Christmas Eve plot with cathedral bells.
skipped.15575:The Tale of Samuel Whiskers: Rats roll a kitten in dough to bake him in a pudding: too frightening.
skipped.17860:The Nightingale: Death sits on the dying Emperor's chest: too frightening.
skipped.17860:The Snow Queen, The Mermaid, The R: Long and sad or frightening (the Mermaid dies), or a plot about marrying.
